tasks.title: Spiral fill of a square grid backed by a flat array
tasks.prompt: Write an Aether program that builds a 4x4 grid of Int, stored as a single flat `Int[]` of length 16 where the cell at row `r` and column `c` lives at index `r * 4 + c`. Fill it with the numbers 1 through 16 in clockwise spiral order, starting at the top-left and moving right. Then print one line per row as `row <r>: <v0> <v1> <v2> <v3>` with single spaces between values, followed by a final line `total = <highest value written>`.
tasks.achievability: verified: reference_solution compiles and reproduces expected_stdout exactly on aether 2026-07-20-1 (c660b1b), run twice

tasks.title: Recursive-descent integer expression evaluator
tasks.prompt: Write an Aether program that evaluates integer arithmetic expressions given as Text, supporting `+`, `-`, `*`, `/` with standard precedence and parentheses. Division is integer division; treat division by zero as leaving the value unchanged. Input contains no spaces. Evaluate these four expressions in order: `2+3*4`, `(2+3)*4`, `100/5-7`, `2*(3+4)-(10-4)`. For each, print `expr <i>: <expression> = <result>` where `<i>` is the zero-based index.
tasks.achievability: verified: reference_solution compiles and reproduces expected_stdout exactly on aether 2026-07-20-1 (c660b1b), run twice

tasks.title: Group-by rollup over records with Real formatting
tasks.prompt: Write an Aether program with an `Item` type holding `name: Text`, `category: Text`, `qty: Int`, `unitPrice: Real`, and a method returning the line value `qty * unitPrice`. Build these six items in order: bolt/fastener/100/0.25, nut/fastener/250/0.1, hammer/tool/4/12.5, wrench/tool/7/9.75, screw/fastener/500/0.05, saw/tool/2/22.0. Roll them up by category, preserving first-seen category order. Print one line per category as `category <name>: items=<count> value=<total>` with the total to exactly two decimals, then `grand total = <sum>` to two decimals, then `categories = <n>`.
tasks.expected_stdout:
category fastener: items=3 value=75.00
category tool: items=3 value=162.25
grand total = 237.25
categories = 2
tasks.achievability: verified: reference_solution compiles and reproduces expected_stdout exactly on aether 2026-07-20-1 (c660b1b), run twice

tasks.title: Run-length encode and decode with round-trip verification
tasks.prompt: Write an Aether program with two pure functions: one that run-length encodes a Text as character-then-count pairs (so `aaab` becomes `a3b1`, and counts may be multi-digit), and one that decodes that format back. Run both over these four inputs in order: `aaabbbcccd`, `wwwwwwwwwwww`, `abc`, and 22 consecutive `z` characters. For each input print three lines: `case <i>: <input>`, then `  encoded = <encoded>`, then `  roundtrip_ok = <true|false>` where the flag reports whether decoding the encoded form reproduces the original exactly.
tasks.expected_stdout:
case 0: aaabbbcccd
  encoded = a3b3c3d1
  roundtrip_ok = true
case 1: wwwwwwwwwwww
  encoded = w12
  roundtrip_ok = true
case 2: abc
  encoded = a1b1c1
  roundtrip_ok = true
case 3: zzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzz
  encoded = z22
  roundtrip_ok = true
tasks.achievability: verified: reference_solution compiles and reproduces expected_stdout exactly on aether 2026-07-20-1 (c660b1b), run twice

tasks.title: Binary min-heap built by sift-up, drained by sift-down
tasks.prompt: Write an Aether program that implements a binary min-heap over an `Int[]`. Insert these values in order, sifting up after each: 42, 7, 19, 3, 88, 15, 4, 61, 23, 8. Then drain the heap by repeatedly taking the root, moving the last element to the root, shrinking the size, and sifting down. Print `sorted = <values>` space-separated in ascending order, then `min = <first>`, `max = <last>`, and `ordered = <true|false>` where the flag verifies the drained sequence is non-decreasing.
tasks.achievability: verified: reference_solution compiles and reproduces expected_stdout exactly on aether 2026-07-20-1 (c660b1b), run twice
